facts.raw_span: Visual acuity: 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes (OU)
Few yellow spots present, no pigmentary degeneration
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades
Large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region
Visual acuity: 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes (OU)
Few yellow spots present, no pigmentary degeneration
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades
Large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region

concepts.why: The patient's night blindness since childhood, flat rod electroretinogram, and complete loss of photoreceptors in the superotemporal region are consistent with Retinitis pigmentosa.
The superotemporal zones showing hypofluorescence and complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in the superotemporal region suggest Choroidal dystrophy.
The large, slow scotopic and photopic responses and flat rod electroretinogram are consistent with Cone-rod dystrophy.
The superotemporal zones showing hypofluorescence and central macula with clear OCT layers are consistent with Stargardt disease.
The patient's night blindness since childhood and flat rod electroretinogram are consistent with Leber congenital amaurosis.
The patient's Goldmann visual field showing an inferonasal scotoma is explained by retinal dystrophy.

rationales.F01: Night blindness since childhood is a strong indicator of retinal dystrophy and related conditions.
rationales.F07: Inferonasal scotoma is a moderate indicator of retinitis pigmentosa and cone-rod dystrophy.
rationales.F09: Flat rod electroretinogram is a strong indicator of retinitis pigmentosa and related conditions.
rationales.F11: Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region is a strong indicator of retinitis pigmentosa and related conditions.

frontier_selector.rationale: Night blindness since childhood, flat rod electroretinogram, and complete loss of photoreceptors in the superotemporal region support Retinitis pigmentosa, with Cone-rod dystrophy as a close runner-up due to similar electroretinogram findings and visual field defects.
